description.to:
Outcome: amplify/storage/resource.ts gives the editor and admin groups read, write and delete on all of media/* and newsroom/*, and guests read media/*; nothing mentions a tenant, and the identity pool cannot tell one tenant's folder from another (docs/multi-tenancy.md, "Story pictures and the one-key rule"). On the shared stack: uploads use a short-lived presigned URL issued by a function that checks the tenant (the model-attachment-upload function already follows this pattern), keys move under tenants/<tenant>/ (media, newsroom, corpora, preview), the identity pool grants tenant users no direct S3 access, and public images are served only through CloudFront from the site prefix. The one-key rule becomes tenants/<tenant>/media/<srcPath>; papyrus_content.renditions.media_key_for_source is the single place that builds it. copy-backend --stamp-tenant and import-markus already write media/<tenant>/..., which PPY-8f9462 reconciles.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/storage/resource.ts, amplify/functions/model-attachment-upload/, amplify/functions/renditions/ (source key parsing), amplify/publication/renditions-function.ts, src/papyrus_content/renditions.py (media_key_for_source), the newsroom image upload code path (components/ and app/newsroom using Amplify Storage uploadData), docs/multi-tenancy.md.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-storage-isolation.feature):
Scenario: An editor cannot write another tenant's object
    Given an "alpha" editor
    When the editor asks for an upload URL for "tenants/beta/media/assets/x/pic.png"
    Then the request is refused

Scenario: An uploaded picture gets renditions under its tenant
    Given an "alpha" editor uploads "assets/launch/pic.png"
    When the renditions function runs
    Then the renditions are under the alpha site prefix and nowhere else

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-0bb0fd. Blocks PPY-bdc4ee. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-5e0259.

Testing: Unit tests of the key builder and the upload function; Behave in a sandbox; adversarial suite covers presign, direct identity-pool access and rendition paths.
Rollout: Shared stack first. Dedicated sites keep the current rules until they adopt their tenant (PPY-13fbea); the key function supports both layouts during the move.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: existing pictures lose their renditions when keys move (the PPY-a96347 failure). Mitigation: the move is a copy plus row update with the existing repair command (stories repair-image-paths) and a dry run listing every object first.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: changes: storage access rules (identity-pool policies).
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
